answer_1.quote: We experiment with various state-of-the-art pretrained summarization models, namely T5 and BART, and Large Language Models (LLMs) including OpenAI's gpt-3.5-turbo (the model behind Chat-GPT) ... We thus generate the dataset D4 that contains the LLM-generated summaries of documents in D3. ... We input the old and new versions of the law articles changed by the amendment to an LLM ... and ask it to generate a possible sentence for the position paper of a lobby ... Hence, we automatically translate all the non-English speeches to English by using the open-source OPUS-MT models ...
answer_1.outputs: Summaries of lobby documents and MEP speeches; generated amendment positions; translations of MEP speeches

answer_4.quote: We manually compare five random summaries generated by each model and find that ChatGPT and Vicuna generate coherent summaries that capture the most salient points expressed in the document, while T5 and BART omit important information and generate disconnected sentences that are almost the same as those in the original document. ... Two of the authors independently performed the labeling.
answer_4.guideline: Comparison of summaries generated by different models to assess coherence and salience
